transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-04
Start: 09:43 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (Starlight CTO), Ben Torres (Platform Lead), Rene Alvarez (Security), Maya Ortiz (Product)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Quick walkthrough of Redwood model catalog and how to pick open models for clinical triage and internal summarization.
- Discussed benchmarks (latency, cost per 1k tokens), compatibility matrix (quantization, GPU types, 8k vs 32k contexts), and private deployment options (VPC, KMS).
- Agreed next steps: share deck, run perf estimate for 8k contexts, schedule POC scoping.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya patel from redwood, i'm the account exec on this. liam is our se, he'll drive the demo and perf stuff.
[00:18] Dr. Aisha Khan: thanks maya, we're excited, short intro — i'm aisha, cto at starlight, we own clinical workflows and triage. ben will talk infra.
[00:28] Ben Torres: yep, ben here, platform lead. we run k8s on gcp, interested in latency targets ~200ms p95 for short assistants.
[00:36] Liam Chen: awesome, i'll jump into the model catalog — quick note, i'll show a mix of open models we curate and how redwood surfaces perf profiles and compatibility. some ASR in transcript might be off, sorry for typos.
[01:05] Liam Chen: first screen, model catalog: filters on task (chat, summarization, embeddings), size, architecture, verified perf. you can sort by latency, cost, or quality. for open models we show quantized variants too — 4-bit, 8-bit, and float16.
[01:38] Rene Alvarez: quick question — how do you surface soc 2 or encryption info per model? we need to know key management details.
[01:46] Maya Patel: good Q. we don't change model crypto but we attach deployment-level controls: private deployments integrate with customer KMS/HSM, audit logs, and RBAC. liam will show the compatibility matrix which flags KMS-ready builds.
[02:10] Liam Chen: right — compatibility matrix: columns are model family, quantization support, recommended GPU (A100, H100, T4 for small), max supported context (8k, 32k), and notes on performance delta when using quantized kernels. it's available as CSV export.
[02:45] Dr. Aisha Khan: do you have benchmark numbers for 8k context models? our docs need longer context for chart review summarization.
[02:53] Liam Chen: yes — we maintain per-model perf profiles. eg: Open-Long-8k (quantized 4-bit) on H100: ~180ms p95 for a single-stream 512-token decode; cost per 1k tokens about $0.07 with continuous batching. float16 variant is ~20% higher latency. i'll attach the benchmark sheet after.
[03:22] Ben Torres: are those numbers from your hosted infra or dedicated? because our network to hosted endpoints adds ~30-50ms.
[03:30] Maya Patel: great point — benchmarks are labeled by deployment mode: hosted (shared), dedicated (reserved pools), private (customer VPC). we include network delta estimates and recommend running a short fenced benchmark during POC since egress and regional hops matter.
[03:55] Liam Chen: moving on — model selection criteria: we recommend picking models by task fidelity first (eval sets), then compute profile. for triage/summarization we often propose mid-sized LLMs that have high instruction-following on clinical prompt sets — they hit a sweet spot on cost/latency.
[04:28] Dr. Aisha Khan: when you say "eval sets" are those public GLUE-style or your own clinical sets?
[04:34] Liam Chen: both. redwood runs internal evals and customers can upload prompt sets. we support per-prompt quality monitoring and regression alerts — we hook those to your evaluation prompts to watch for regressions on new model variants.
[04:58] Rene Alvarez: security follow-up — for private deployment, do we keep model weights in our VPC?
[05:04] Maya Patel: yes — private deployments are customer-hosted or VPC peering. weights can be pulled into your environment and keys stay with your KMS. audit logs stream to your SIEM.
[05:18] Ben Torres: good. can you talk about fallback policies — if a large model exceeds latency we want automated fallback to cheaper model.
[05:26] Liam Chen: built-in routing policies can do model tiering — e.g., policy route for p95 < 200ms to small-variant, else route to cached responses or a cheaper quantized model. you can set thresholds per route.
[05:48] Maya Ortiz: do customers see a compatibility matrix per release? wondering about rolling quantization changes.
[05:55] Liam Chen: yes, compatibility is versioned. we map kernels and quantization flags to model versions and runtime kernels; the console exposes a compatibility matrix and a "model variants" pane so you can pin to specific kernel+quantization combos.
[06:20] Dr. Aisha Khan: latency vs cost tradeoff question: we care about cost but can't compromise too much on accuracy for triage. what are typical accuracy deltas when moving from float16 to 4-bit quant?
[06:29] Liam Chen: depends on model family. in our evals, for the open families we recommend, 4-bit quant usually shows <2-3% drop in instruction-following and some degradation on long-context math-like reasoning. we always suggest evaluation on a customer prompt set first.
[06:52] Ben Torres: could you show the console quickly — where we pick model and see perf numbers?
[06:58] Liam Chen: sure, switching screen — Console -> Model Catalog -> select model -> performance tab. here you see historical latency distribution, cost estimate per 1k tokens, and compatibility flags. note the little "run benchmark" button which spins up a small dedicated test to measure exact numbers from your region.
[07:28] Dr. Aisha Khan: the run benchmark, does it require dedicated capacity purchase?
[07:33] Maya Patel: no — we offer short benchmark credits for evals; for larger sustained tests we'd recommend a short dedicated reservation, but the quick benchmark is on hosted infra and gives representative numbers.
[07:50] Ben Torres: regarding throughput: what batching behavior does Redwood use? we have bursty traffic with many concurrent short requests.
[07:58] Liam Chen: runtime uses continuous batching and adaptive batching windows; in dedicated pools you can tune batch size and target latency. for bursty short requests we recommend prefix caching + small per-route batch windows to keep p95 low while still getting batching benefits.
[08:20] Maya Patel: also mention model caching — if you have repeated prefixes (patient instructions), KV cache helps a lot with cost.
[08:30] Rene Alvarez: audit and logs — what fields are in the audit logs? need to avoid patient PHI being logged.
[08:37] Maya Patel: by default we mask PII in hosted, but for private deployments you control logging. we have a log redaction feature, and you can route full logs to your SIEM under your retention policy. we'll share a sample network diagram and logging schema.
[09:02] Liam Chen: back to catalog — here's an example compatibility table row: ModelX-1.2 | quantized: 4-bit yes | GPUs: H100/A100 recommended | max ctx: 32k (chunking supported) | notes: struggles with long numeric sequences.
[09:26] Dr. Aisha Khan: chunking for 32k — how seamless is that in the SDK?
[09:32] Liam Chen: SDK has built-in chunking helpers and you can enable automatic stitching in the runtime. that's currently beta but widely used by customers doing chart summarization.
[09:48] Ben Torres: SSO and IAM — how does enrollment work for engineers to access the console in private mode?
[09:54] Maya Patel: Private control plane supports SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC. you can limit model deploy permissions and route creation.
[10:05] Dr. Aisha Khan: any redwood-verified clinical models in the catalog?
[10:10] Liam Chen: we have curated model families with clinical evaluation labels, but not "clinically approved." we provide evaluation results and you run your compliance reviews. some customers share prompt sets and we run private evals as part of POC.
[10:30] Maya Ortiz: curious about model rollouts — we want canarying and automatic rollback on metric regression.
[10:36] Liam Chen: rollouts: console supports canary deploys, A/B, and automatic fallback. you can tie regressions to your eval set and set thresholds to auto-roll back to previous variant.
[10:58] Ben Torres: pricing — rough idea of hosted vs dedicated cost?
[11:04] Maya Patel: high level: hosted pay-as-you-go per-token and per-embedding; dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commitment but lower unit cost. Optimize gives recommendations on quantization and batching to cut unit price. we'll send a pricing appendix.
[11:24] Dr. Aisha Khan: procurement question — any long lead times for private deployments?
[11:30] Maya Patel: private deployments depend on environment — VPC peering is fastest (weeks), full on-prem with HSM can take longer. we have a checklist we'll share.
[11:48] Liam Chen: quick demo of the benchmark sheet — here's a per-model row: model id, deployment mode, p50/p95/p999, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, notes. you can filter by gpu type.
[12:12] Ben Torres: for our SLOs, we need p95 < 200ms for short assistant (<512 tokens). do you have recommended model candidates?
[12:20] Liam Chen: yes — candidate list: ModelA-small-llm (good for short assistant, 120ms p95 on A100), ModelB-mid (higher quality, 220ms p95), ModelC-long (32k ctx, 300ms p95). we'll propose a shortlist in the deck.
[12:45] Dr. Aisha Khan: can you run a POC where we send real workload with scrubbed PHI?
[12:51] Maya Patel: absolutely — we often do scrubbed real-data POCs. we'll provide guidelines on redaction and a secure upload flow.
[13:08] Liam Chen: technical caveat: quantization kernels for certain open-model families are still experimental on some runtimes — we'll flag those in the compatibility matrix.
[13:27] Rene Alvarez: do you do penetration testing on private deployments?
[13:31] Maya Patel: yes, we provide guidance and have a third-party pentest report for our managed control plane; for private deployments we can sign an SOW for pentest support.
[13:46] Ben Torres: what about model updates — if redwood updates a model, how do we control rollouts?
[13:52] Liam Chen: model updates are versioned and we push them as "model variants". customers can opt into auto-updates or pin to a specific variant. the console gives a diff and known-regression flags.
[14:10] Dr. Aisha Khan: any limitations on embeddings for our search product? we use dense embeddings at scale.
[14:16] Liam Chen: embeddings are supported; we have optimized embedding runners with batching and lower memory footprints. we expose throughput and cost numbers by model.
[14:34] Maya Ortiz: what does the onboarding look like?
[14:37] Maya Patel: onboarding: 1) quick pilot on hosted for evaluation, 2) POC with private staging if needed, 3) ramp to dedicated or private based on results. SE and solutions engineering help set SLOs and run benchmarks.
[14:58] Ben Torres: can you share a sample compatibility CSV now?
[15:02] Liam Chen: shared in chat: /link/model-catalog-compatibility.csv (note: link is ephemeral).
[15:18] Dr. Aisha Khan: ok let's talk timing — we'd like to run a pilot in January and ramp in Q1.
[15:25] Maya Patel: that's great. next steps recap in the chat — i'll send the deck, the compatibility matrix, and the benchmark spreadsheet. liam will run the perf estimate and we'll schedule POC scoping with ben.
[15:45] Ben Torres: one last infra detail — do you support private link into our GCP project?
[15:51] Maya Patel: yes, we support VPC peering and private link patterns; we'll share network diagram and requirements.
[16:05] Rene Alvarez: make sure to include redaction and logging schema in what you share.
[16:12] Maya Patel: noted, we'll attach log schema and redaction guide.
[16:24] Liam Chen: quickly show "Optimize" tab — shows suggested quantization and batching settings, estimated unit cost savings, and quality delta estimates based on eval sets. it's useful to decide which model variant to choose.
[16:48] Dr. Aisha Khan: can Optimize run automatically on our eval set and recommend a variant?
[16:54] Liam Chen: yes, Optimize can run a sweep and recommend quant+batch settings with an estimated quality-cost curve; we can surface only recommendations that meet your accuracy constraints.
[17:10] Maya Ortiz: if we do the POC, who will be our main contact?
[17:14] Maya Patel: i'll be primary AE, liam SE for technical; ben we'll work with your infra, rene on security.
[17:28] Ben Torres: ok, thanks.
[17:31] Maya Patel: wrap up — recap next steps and i'll drop items in CRM. any final q's?
[17:38] Dr. Aisha Khan: none from me. thanks for the thorough runthrough.
[17:42] Maya Patel: great, we'll follow up by monday with the artifacts. thanks everyone.

Call ended at ~10:31 UTC

Post-call notes (auto):
